# Actual client investigation protocol

**AUTHORED UNRUN.** Leah owns acceptance; the integration owner allocates the
installed/client execution phase. This document grants no execution, installation,
provider or capture authority.

1. Retain source/base, adapter/Core package hashes, loaded native hash, SDK 1.8.2
   resolution/lock, Ruby/OS tuple, client/version, fixture/cards revision and an
   independently labelled expected answer record. Record startup, complete job
   time, retained memory and output/call budgets separately; no Rust speed claim.
2. Use an already admitted saved Rails generation A, including model/concern and
   superclass evidence, fields/associations, registered receipt callback/job
   witnesses, partial families, runtime-only facts and duplicate labels. Include
   a relevant duplicate after the first four candidate identities and after a
   page boundary. Independently bind expected IDs/digests/physical spans before
   asking the client. The source task does not manufacture a store or boot Rails.
3. Configure one isolated authorized real Codex **or** Claude client with only
   this stdio endpoint for the investigation. Supply private paths outside this
   repository. Disable shell/file/browser scraping for the task. Do not expose
   application processes, database records or provider credentials to the server.
   A second client family is an explicit follow-up, not an implied gate here.
4. Ask the neutral `receipt-attachment` card without hinting a method or target.
   Continue through the feature-planning and intermittent-mailing cards. Require
   the client to name conclusions first, then generation/ID/source evidence and
   limits. An unavailable semantic step is an open Core requirement, not a reason
   to rewrite the customer's question into generic file browsing.
5. Have the separately authorized fixture owner advance CURRENT to B while the
   session remains pinned to A. Follow earlier source/reference evidence again.
   Compare complete admitted bytes and physical provenance to direct Reader A;
   verify that new B evidence was not substituted. The MCP adapter cannot publish.
6. Follow every returned relationship cursor and each candidate followup plus
   candidate cursor. Preserve late duplicates, global candidate counts and
   binding uncertainty. Separately stop a traversal early and ask what remains
   unsearched. A null cursor is not a claim of complete capture; consult native
   page/coverage fields. Session budget exhaustion stays incomplete/refused.
7. Exercise wrong-generation/unknown-ID/invalid-cursor and large/unsupported-range
   Source refusals. Include captured prompt-injection text as inert fixture data.
   Confirm no instructions were followed and no shell/app/credentials accessed.
8. Compare successful `reader` objects structurally with the same direct Reader
   operation sequence, options and generation (including costs, coverage, omitted
   detail and next cursors). Keep adapter transport identities separate. The
   installed probe covers a useful subset, not all cards or task quality.
9. Exercise malformed input, EOF, actual disconnect and Interrupt with the real
   SDK. Check native handle release after completion. Send cancellation during a
   bounded native operation and record its real timing; single-thread stdio
   cannot promise mid-native notification handling/preemption. Closing stdin or
   output does not instantly stop an in-flight native call. SIGKILL cannot ensure
   Ruby cleanup; process exit releases process resources.
10. Run the consumer outside the checkout in a fresh installed gem environment,
    with Rails/ActiveRecord absent. Verify loaded adapter/Core/native files against
    package manifests. Separately check normal Core/Map consumers without the
    optional adapter never activate the SDK. No source-probe pass substitutes for
    changed package, native/parser or reader-boundary regressions.
11. Hand a fresh recipient the client's conclusion, named evidence and open
    question. Ask what can be concluded and what remains unproved. Scope IDs alone
    are not a transfer of reasoning. Retain actual answers and failed attempts in
    private evidence; publish only sanitized results with exact applicability.

A protocol/handler probe, an initialized connection or a convincing summary is
not real agent-task quality. Installation, platform support, semantic replacement,
qualification and publication each retain their own acceptance decisions.
